title: Phase diagram of one-dimensional bosons with Rydberg-dressed soft-core interactions
abstract: Rydberg and Rydberg-dressed atomic gases have recently emerged as a promising quantum simulator for a variety of models in condensed matter physics. Here we investigate one-dimensional bosons with soft-core Rydberg-dressed interactions using exact path-integral quantum Monte Carlo simulations. The finite-range and the negative Fourier component of the interaction potential generate a roton mode at finite momentum, while particle-hole backscattering processes enhance the susceptibility of one-dimensional systems at twice the Fermi momentum. The competition between the corresponding length scales yields a rich phase diagram, featuring a conventional Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) regime, a beyond-TLL regime, and commensurate cluster phases. In the TLL regime, the system transitions from Lieb-Liniger-like bnehavior with Luttinger parameter $K>1$ to hard-rod-like behavior with $K<1$, with a quasi-supersolid phase emerging for $K < 1/2$. For strong interactions and high densities, deviations from TLL theory appear as precursors for the onset of cluster phases, where particles aggregate into stable clusters of several particles. The properties of each phase is discussed in detail.
summary: The paper uses advanced Quantum Monte Carlo simulations to map the phase diagram of 1D bosons with soft-core interactions mimicking Rydberg dressing. It reveals a complex sequence of phases—including TLL, quasi-supersolid, and cluster states—driven by the interplay between interaction range and density. This work is crucial for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in synthetic atomic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex phase diagram of one-dimensional bosons interacting via soft-core Rydberg-dressed potentials.
main_result: The system exhibits a rich sequence of phases, transitioning from Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) behavior through quasi-supersolid regimes to distinct cluster phases under strong interactions.
method: Exact path-integral Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations were employed in continuous space to calculate correlation functions and determine the Luttinger parameter K.
model_or_system: The system models 1D spinless bosons interacting via a soft-core potential derived from Rydberg dressing. The Hamiltonian is analyzed for its competition between roton-driven ordering and particle-hole backscattering processes.
key_observables: Luttinger parameter K, single/pair correlation functions ($g_1, g_2$), static structure factor $S(q)$, and cluster proportions ($	ext{n}_{	ext{cluster}}$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U_0$), density ($n$), Fermi momentum ($k_F$), and the resulting Luttinger parameter K (which dictates regimes like $K>1$, $K<1$, $K<1/2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on QMC simulations, which are compared against theoretical frameworks like TLL theory and Bogoliubov approximations.
figures_summary: Figures map the quantum phase diagram across interaction strength and density, illustrating transitions between LL-like ($K>1$), HR-like ($K<1$), quasi-supersolid ($K < 1/2$), beyond-TLL, and cluster lobes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical context using Rydberg gases, details the QMC methodology for calculating correlation functions, analyzes the resulting equation of state $n(\mu)$, and systematically maps out the phase diagram by tracking changes in the Luttinger parameter K across different interaction regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical map of quantum phases in low-dimensional systems using modern atomic platforms (Rydberg atoms), bridging concepts from TLL theory, supersolidity, and cluster physics.
